messages.author: ee8d003a3bde0676
messages.subject: Error: 'spde' not found
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run the R package SPASIBA (that uses the INLA model) on a linux cluster but faced the following problem:

/home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /usr/lib64/libstdc++.so.6: version `GLIBCXX_3.4.15' not found (required by /home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher)

/home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher)

/home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/libgsl.so.19)

Error in fmesher.read(prefix, "manifold") :

File '/home/svu/dbsnyxe/TMP/RtmpRfo6x8/fmesher19ad1bef7985.manifold' does not exist.


From previous forum posts, it was recommended to run the following line as a workaround:
INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround() 

However, after running the workaround, the following error appears:
Error in INLA::f(spatial, model = spde.infcov, replicate = r) : 
  object 'spde' not found
Calls: SPASIBA.inf ... inla.interpret.formula -> eval -> eval -> <Anonymous>

As spde is part of INLA, I hope someone can enlighten me as to where the error lies.

Thanks

Regards,
Elize

messages.subject: Re: Error: 'spde' not found
parts:

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Error: 'spde' not found
parts:
On Wed, 2016-11-02 at 19:23 -0700, Lilnet Cloud wrote:
> Additionally, the IT department managing the linux cluster was unable
> to clone the source code to complie binary that was provided at https
> ://bitbucket.org/hrue/r-inla
> Will it be possible to obtain a working source code to complie the
> binaries so as to run INLA without using the workaround as the linux
> cluster does not have libc.so.6 and libstdc++.so.6 that are supported
> by the precomplied binaries.

you can download the directory that I use to build the binary from 

www.math.ntnu.no/~hrue/hfiles/build64.tgz


edit the GNUmakefile.

if you do not need the libR support (ie using the model 'rgeneric'),
then you can set these variables to empty

RINC = -DINLA_EXPERIMENTAL -I/usr/share/R/include
RLIB = -L/usr/lib/R/lib -lR 


type make, and make each library listed (like  `make metis' etc), 
at the end do a 'make update'

on ubuntu, there is an easier option, but I guess this is not what you
have


H


--
Håvard Rue

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Error: 'spde' not found
parts:
Hi,

I have run into the same issue:  

Something like this but I wasn't able to capture the specific language.

home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher)

/home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /home/svu/dbsnyxe/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/libgsl.so.19)

The work around INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround() is not working for me and I have tried it in several different ways in addition to those you have recommended in other discussions. I suspect that maybe this did work, but now R tells me that program inla sent an error and I should used verbose = TRUE to see the full description. However, this option in not part of the SPASIBA.inf() function. Rather they made an inla verbose options: verbose.inf=TRUE but tis option does not give any more information. 

The binary build you shared in your reply here no longer exists. 

I'd really like to be able to use this on my university server. Any help is appreciated.

Example code that works on desktop but not server:

library(dplyr)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(RandomFields)
library(INLA)
library(SPASIBA)
library(geosphere)

setwd("/SPASIBA_data")
data<-read.csv("data.csv",header=1)

unk<-slice(data, 1:1)
ref<-filter(data,!sampleID %in% unk$sampleID)

geno.ref<-ref[10:127]
geno.unknown<-unk[10:127]
coord.ref<-ref[c(6,5)]
unk_loc <-unk[c(1,6,5)]

coord.ref<-as.matrix(coord.ref)
geno.ref<-as.matrix(geno.ref)
geno.unknown<-as.matrix(geno.unknown)

size.pop.ref<-read.table("size.pop.ref")
size.pop.ref<-rbind.data.frame(size.pop.ref,size.pop.ref,size.pop.ref,size.pop.ref)
size.pop.ref<-slice(size.pop.ref,1:nrow(geno.ref))
size.pop.ref<-select(size.pop.ref,1:ncol(geno.ref))
size.pop.ref<-as.matrix(size.pop.ref)

INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround()

spa_result <- SPASIBA.inf(geno.ref=geno.ref,
                             ploidy=2,
                             coord.ref=coord.ref,
                             sphere=FALSE, 
                             size.pop.ref=size.pop.ref,
                             geno.unknown=geno.unknown,
                             make.inf=TRUE,
                             loc.infcov = 1:30,
                             make.pred=TRUE,
                             make.assign=TRUE)

Thanks, 

Kristen

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Error: 'spde' not found
parts:
Hi,

the reason is old system libraries on the linux machine you're using.

https://inla.r-inla-download.org/Linux-builds/

contains alternative Linux builds, and you can try one of them (try the
CentOS one first). the default build is the Ubunutu 1804.

the HOWTO file, explains what to do.

Let me know if that does not work.

H
